Grandpa Gave 3 Kids $1,000. Who Won?

2026-11-25

Subscribe for one money story a week

About this video

What if you invested $1,000 in the S&P 500 in 1996, or kept it in a cookie jar? Grandpa's three grandkids found out. Thirty years ago, Grandpa Joe gave his three grandkids $1,000 each and one rule: come back in 30 years. Mia spent it. Ben hid it in a cookie jar. Rosie planted a "money tree": an index fund that owns America's 500 biggest companies. Who won? A money story for the whole family. The kids are made up; every number is real. 0:00 Thirty years later 0:35 1996: three envelopes 1:11 Spend, save, or plant 1:56 The first storm 2:44 The biggest storm 3:42 The sneaky mouse 4:36 The weird storm 5:13 Reunion day 6:31 Mia's second chance 7:32 Three lessons The real numbers: - $1,000 in the S&P 500 with dividends reinvested on Nov 25, 1996 was worth $16,368 on Nov 23, 2026 (before fees and taxes). Along the way it fell to $1,117 (Oct 2002), $1,103 (Mar 2009) and $4,591 (Mar 2020). - Prices rose 2.13 times since Nov 1996 (CPI), so $1,000 in a jar now buys what $470 bought then. - $100 a month from Oct 2007: $23,000 put in, worth $100,324 today (it was $1,067 on $1,800 put in at the March 2009 low). Which grandkid are you? Tell me in the comments. Data: S&P 500 Total Return index (Yahoo Finance ^SP500TR); CPI-U, all items (U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics via FRED, CPIAUCSL). Past results don't promise future returns. This video is for education only and is not financial advice. Original story, characters and animation. Narrated with an AI voice.
